chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskan, from Saeed al-Roumy, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) pelted the Great Jamarah, so he saw the people standing still. So he stood up in their midst, then called out in a loud voice: 'O people! This is not a standing stop!' three times. So I did it (as well).

key_terms.الْجَمْرَةَ الْعُظْمَى: The Great Jamarah (the largest pillar in Mina)

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about standing at the Jamarah during stoning?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) actively corrected the common misconception of treating the Jamarah site as a stationary place of prolonged supplication (waqf), emphasizing that the ritual requires movement and brevity rather than lingering. This narration highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on distinguishing between the physical act of stoning and the spiritual state of presence, ensuring the ritual is performed with the speed and intentionality prescribed by the Prophet. It serves as a practical guide for pilgrims to avoid innovations (bid'ah) in Hajj rituals by adhering to the Sunnah of swift action.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad,f rom Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Ibn Muskan, from Saeed Al Roumy who said,

‘Abu Abdullahasws pelted Al-Jamarah Al-Uzmah (the bigger Jamarah), so heasws saw the people having paused. So heasws stood up in their midst, then called out in a loud voice of hisasws: ‘O you people! This is not a Pausing Stop!’ – three times. So I did it (as well)’.
en.sarwar: 5. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Sinan from ibn Muskan from Sa‘id al- Rumiy who has said the following: “

Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, threw pebbles on al-Jamarah al-‘Uzma’ and saw people standing. He (the Imam) stood in their middle and announced with the height of his voice, ‘O people, this is not a station’, three times, and I did it (as he (the Imam) had done).”
